full_judgment: 6. Heard the submissions of the learned DAG and considered the materials on record. It is the admitted position that the accused-petitioner filed the said Power of Attorney before the Assistant Commissioner, Land, Narayanganj in a mutation proceeding for correction of record of rights in their favour. It has been decided by our Apex Court that the Revenue Officer acting in mutation case under section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 ("the said Act") is not a court as he just does an inquiry in the said proceeding. In Shahera Khatun's case cited above, the Appellate Division distinguished between two proceedings, namely the proceeding under section 143 (maintenance of record of rights) and the proceedings under section 144 (revision of the record of rights) of the said Act and held that a Revenue Officer acting in mutation cases under section 143 of the said Act is not a Court, although the same officer acting in a proceeding under section 144 of the said Act is a court in view of Rule 39 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955. Therefore, filing of forged documents before the Revenue Officer acting under section 143 in mutation proceeding, as in the present case, does not invoke the bar under section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure and in such a case the court can take cognizance on the Petition of Complaint filed by a private person.
